newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMF's Camdessus to visit S.Africa Thursday.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus to visit S.Africa Thursday.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director Michael Camdessus, making his first official visit to South Africa, will meet President Nelson Mandela, businessmen and labour leaders on Thursday and Friday, an official said.

Finance Ministry spokeswoman Jennifer Wilson said Camdessus would meet Mandela, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and (central) Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals in Johannesburg, before flying to Cape Town on Friday.
"He was here for the UNCTAD meeting earlier this year, but this is his first official visit to South Africa. It is in line with his programme of visiting all IMF member states," she said.
She said Camdessus and Manuel would address a news conference late on Friday.
Camdessus met Manuel and some officials during his April visit to the U.N. trade body, UNCTAD, in April and pronounced post-apartheid South Africa "an extraordinary success story".
Wilson said Manuel invited Camdessus to South Africa during the annual meeting of the IMF in Washington earlier this month.
South Africa initiated negotiations there for the country's first IMF loan, which director general of finance Maria Ramos said could be denominated in rands.
The $67 million loan would be for a single industrial competitiveness and job creation project giving small exporters access to technical help, she said.
